review_notes:
I read the whole file (the two theorems `exactK0_ofLinearCharacter_one` and `exactK0_ofLinearCharacter_mul`). I also read the relevant rules in Ring.lean and LinearCharacter/Basic.lean. `fdRepK0RingEquiv_of` is `@[simp]` and its left side is `fdRepK0RingEquiv k G (ExactK0.of V)` for any `V : FDRep k G`. That pattern matches the left sides of both target lemmas, so the file's comment is right that simp would rewrite them first. Tagging them `@[simp]` would therefore most likely fail `simpNF`, and the simp-normal form of the left side would be an `asModule` expression that is awkward to use.

`FDRep.ofLinearCharacter_def` is deliberately not simp. Its right side `FDRep.of (Representation.ofLinearCharacter χ)` is a more exposed form, and the library's stated implementation notes say consumers should not unfold the definition. `Representation.ofLinearCharacter_one` is already `@[simp]`, and the file uses it only inside an explicit `rw`.

I found no competing rules, no rewrite cycle and no wrong-direction rule that I could justify from the sources. A new simp interface, such as a monoid hom from characters into the units of the ring, would be speculative. I did not check every downstream use of these lemmas. I did not run Lean, so everything above is judged from the source text alone.
